messages.subject: Re: Global variables are also shown to other browsers!
messages.subject_clean: Global variables are also shown to other browsers!
messages.body_plain:
Global variables (variables defined outside the server function OR variables that you assign with <<-) are in fact global to everyone. That's not a bug, that's what global variables are meant to do. Have you read through the scoping rules in Shiny? https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html

It's a useful read and might help you with your problem

messages.subject: Re: Shiny always crashes with 3.4.0 on Windows
messages.subject_clean: Shiny always crashes with 3.4.0 on Windows
messages.body_plain:
You should "sudo su - shiny" on the server, then run R, then see what .libPaths() returns. If there's nothing there that's under the shiny user's home directory, then you need to follow the instructions in the doc I linked but as root.

On Wed, May 31, 2017 at 3:42 PM Jesse Bell <bellj...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hey Joe,
>
> Have there been any other findings/updates/inquiries regarding this issue?  We recently upgraded to 3.4.0 and have followed all of the instructions in your writeup (thank you!) and are still having issues across all shiny apps.  It seems that it may be related to reactive functions and/or memory mapping.  We have completely uninstalled R, R-Studio, and all packages and re-installed them, only to get the same segfault errors.  There are no clear error messages for us to use for troubleshooting.  There are some warnings thrown, but nothing that hasn't been thrown before and they don't seem to be real problems, i.e.:
>
> Warning in if (task_ids_a == "redacted string message") { :
>
>   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
>
> Warning in if (task_ids_b == "redacted string message") { :
>
>   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
>
> Using title as id variables
>
> -su: line 1: 45852 Segmentation fault      (core dumped) R --no-save --slave -f \/opt\/shiny-server\/R\/SockJSAdapter\.R
>
> All of the code executes fine via r-studio, but segfaults when executed through shiny-server which again points to some type of memory issue.  Any help, or suggested troubleshooting steps is greatly appreciated.
>
> Cheers and thanks
> On Wednesday, May 31, 2017 at 1:02:58 AM UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > For anyone still dealing with R 3.4.0 upgrade issues (or upgrading to any other version of R, for future readers) we have a writeup here with some practical steps to take:

> >
> > On Monday, May 29, 2017 at 7:47:47 AM UTC-7, Brandon Loudermilk wrote:
> > > I experienced similar problem: Upgraded from R 3.3.3 to 3.4.0 and my shiny app warned then crashed. Attempted to update packages but could not b/c of bug (https://www.mail-archive.com/r-h...@r-project.org/msg243256.html). Installed R-3.4.0 patched build (https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/rtest.html). Updated packages (from within RStudio). Manually removed then install.packages("Cairo"). Shiny app works.

messages.subject: Re: Call startup function prior to Shiny listening on port
messages.subject_clean: Call startup function prior to Shiny listening on port
messages.body_plain:
Add a file called global.R in the same directory as ui.R and server.R. That should be exactly what you need, if you do the load there.

(If you are using Shiny Server Pro and encounter undesirable utilization_scheduler behavior with very slow global.R scripts, please contact sup...@rstudio.com; we have a fix for this problem that is not yet released but available for testing on request.)

messages.subject: Re: How to manipulate reactive expressions like a normal dataframe?
messages.subject_clean: How to manipulate reactive expressions like a normal dataframe?
messages.body_plain:
Write another reactive expression that reads load_table() and performs the various filtering operations on it, and returns the resulting data frame. For example, if input$columns had the names of the columns to show, you'd do

filtered <- reactive({
  df <- load_table()

  # Show only selected columns
  if (!is.null(input$columns)) {
    stopifnot(all(input$columns %in% names(df)))
    df <- df[,input$columns]
  }

  # apply other filters...

  df
})

On Thursday, June 1, 2017 at 3:18:20 AM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> This is fine but in your /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf you need to add two new locations, one for each subdirectory, as siblings to the "location /" block you already have. And they must come before the location /. See below for an example.
>
> The reason this is necessary is because once a Shiny app is found in a parent URL (in this case the URL being requested is http://server:3838/production-apps/ but there's an app in http://server:3838/) the URL is passed to the Shiny app to handle. And since subdirectories of Shiny apps are assumed to be private (unless they have the special name "www") then you get a Not Found error. Adding the additional location directives to eh config, and putting them above the original location directive, explicitly tells Shiny Server to treat those two particular URL paths (and their subpaths) as being distinct from the top-level Shiny app.
>
> Before:
>
> # Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
> run_as shiny;
>
> # Define a server that listens on port 3838
> server {
>   listen 3838;
>
>   # Define a location at the base URL
>   location / {
>
>     # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
>     site_dir /srv/shiny-server;
>
>     # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
>     log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
>
>     # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
>     # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
>     directory_index on;
>   }
> }
>
> After:
>
> # Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
> run_as shiny;
>
> # Define a server that listens on port 3838
> server {
>   listen 3838;
>
>   location /production-apps {
>     site_dir /srv/shiny-server/production-apps;
>     log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
>     directory_index on;
>   }
>
>   location /development-apps {
>     site_dir /srv/shiny-server/development-apps;
>     log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
>     directory_index on;
>   }
>
>   location / {
>
>     # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
>     site_dir /srv/shiny-server;
>
>     # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
>     log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
>
>     # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
>     # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
>     directory_index on;
>   }
> }
>
>
> On Tue, May 30, 2017 at 8:46 AM Clifford Long <crlon...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Dear All,
> >
> > I have a question, if I may.
> >
> > We have developed a growing number of shiny apps that we use often.  ("Thank you!" to the authors of shiny, shiny-server)
> >
> > We host these shiny apps on a Linux server (Red Hat) within our corporate firewall.
> >
> >
> > OUR SYSTEM
> > Red Hat: Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server release 6.9 (Santiago)
> > shiny-server:  Shiny Server v1.3.0.403  Node.js v0.10.21
> > shiny:  1.0.3
> > R:  R version 3.3.3
> >
> >
> > Our setup on the server is based on the shiny-server instructions and basic setup.  We have a folder "opt" which has a matching "srv" folder (apologies if this is redundant ... I'm new to Linux and servers).  Within the 'srv' folder we have the 'shiny-server' folder.  The landing page "index.html" file is in the 'shiny-server' folder along with the css file.  We then created two subfolders, one for production apps ('production-apps') and one for development apps ('development-apps').  We publish links to apps in the 'production-apps' folder on the shiny-server landing page.  This approach has worked well so far.
> >
> >
> > THE ISSUE
> > For the landing page we started with html/css.  We then decided to explore the use of a shiny app and markdown to provide the landing page.  The shiny app uses server.R and ui.R files located within the 'shiny-server' directory (where the 'index.html' file was previously kept).  The UI is based on navbarPage, and each page draws content from an ".md" file.
> >
> > When we used the 'index.html' approach all of the links worked well.
> >
> > When we switched to the shiny app and .md approach for the shiny-server landing page we encountered some difficulty.  We can no longer link to subfolders such as 'development-apps'.  For example, http://10.2.13.27:3838/development-apps/ would provide a directory listing when we use the landing page based on html/css ('index.html').  When we switch to using the shiny navbarpage as the shiny-server landing page we can no longer access this URL path - we get an error message ("Not Found").  We also get this when we link directly to an app directory (http://dev2-deming.essendant.com/production-apps/itbq_facility_report).
> >
> > Is the use of a shiny app (ui.R, server.R) for the shiny-server landing page just not a good practice?  Or is it OK to do this and we are just missing some setting that would allow us to access/link-to shiny-server subdirectories and apps if we use a shiny app for the shiny-server landing page?
> >
> > Thank you in advance for any guidance that might be provided.  And apologies in advance for any shortcoming with the question.
> >
> > Cliff

messages.subject: Re: Shiny always crashes with 3.4.0 on Windows
messages.subject_clean: Shiny always crashes with 3.4.0 on Windows
messages.body_plain:
We had installed everything as root.  Good news is we seem to have found the solution.  It seems that the release of the Just In Time (JIT) compiler as part of 3.4.0 was the culprit.  This seems to be the specific problem related to shiny apps:

https://www.r-statistics.com/2017/04/r-3-4-0-is-released-with-new-speed-upgrades-and-bug-fixes/
("For now, the compiler will not compile code containing explicit calls to browser(): this is to support single stepping from the browser() call.")

Adding the below line to the top of all of our app.R scripts has fixed (knock on wood) the problem.

enableJIT(0)

Thanks to our incredible Data Scientist, David Fackler for combing the release notes of 3.4.0 and putting together the pieces of the puzzle, and thanks to this group for all of the previous posts which helped us troubleshoot.  Hope this is helpful to others.

messages.subject: Re: Offline Shiny Server installation
messages.subject_clean: Offline Shiny Server installation
messages.body_plain:
I think you can probably install it into a VM that matches your distro version, using the packaged installer, and copy out the contents of /opt/shiny-server and put that on your offline machine somehow. You will need to call bin/shiny-server with a single argument that is the path to your shiny-server.conf file, since that will not be in its usual location of /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf. You will also probably get errors about certain directories not being writable, you'll have to use directives in shiny-server.conf to override these paths with ones you have write access to.

messages.subject: Re: R Shiny bi-directional reactive progressive filtering
messages.subject_clean: R Shiny bi-directional reactive progressive filtering
messages.body_plain:
Try taking a look at my example. https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/76cffbbdd9db0b0e971fd34f575fa45b This is an inherently tricky problem, whether you're using reactive or imperative primitives; as exemplified by this comment in my gist:

  # When the other filters change, update this filter to remove rows that
  # are filtered out by the other filters' criteria. (We also add in the
  # currently selected values for this filter, so that changing other
  # filters does not cause this filter's selected values to be unselected;
  # while that behavior might make sense logically, it's a poor user
  # experience.)

On Fri, Jun 2, 2017 at 6:15 AM Garrick McComas <mccomas...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I'm pulling a large dataset down into a Shiny app that I only want to pull once with a reactive function and one mandatory filter. Using the reactiveUI framework, I then want to be able to do progressive filtering on the dataset with a combination of several independent selectizeInput(s) such that the available choices are dictated by the selectizeInput(s) already selected. The kicker is that I'm trying to do this without stipulating any order of operations to the filtering, such that any combination of applied inputs would in turn inform available choices in the other available inputs. I'd also like for the user to get back to the original unfiltered dataset by simply clearing inputs.
>
> In the script below, I've simulated this process with one "mandatory" filter that has to be applied before the full dataset is pulled into Shiny nested in a reactive function. The resultant dataset is then nested in another reactive function where the optional and progressive filtering takes place.
>
> Currently the script momentarily applies a filter before reverting to the full dataset, implying that either some sort of recursion is taking place or the initial reactive function that generates the large dataset is being triggered. I've come across a lot of notes about the use of "isolate" that might be of help here, but I haven't been able to figure out how it might be applied in this case. I'm sure the answer to my issue is buried in some post, but I'm having a very difficult time determining how to fix this issue. I would be most grateful for any help!
>
>
> library(shiny)
> library(dplyr)
> library(ggplot2)
>
> ui <- fluidPage(
>
>     fluidRow(
>         # control panel
>         column(
>             # initial input required to query large dataset
>             numericInput(
>                 inputId = "min_year",
>                 label = "Select Min Model Year",
>                 min = 1999,
>                 max = 2008,
>                 value = 2000
>             ),
>             # progressive manufacturer filter
>             uiOutput("manufacturer_control"),
>             # progressive transmission filter
>             uiOutput("trans_control"),
>             # progressive compact filter
>             uiOutput("cyl_control"),
>             width = 2
>         ),
>         # display table
>         column(
>             tableOutput("table"),
>             width = 10
>         )
>     )
> )
>
> server <- function(input, output) {
>
>     # reactive function to pull down large dataset once
>     mpg_all <- reactive({
>
>         ggplot2::mpg %>% filter(year >= input$min_year)
>     })
>
>     # reactive filtering on large dataset that progressively narrows input choices
>     mpg_fltr <- reactive({
>
>         mpg_fltr <- mpg_all()
>
>         if (!is.null(input$manufacturer)) {
>             mpg_fltr <- filter(mpg_fltr, manufacturer %in% input$maufacturer)
>         }
>
>         if (!is.null(input$trans)) {
>             mpg_fltr <- filter(mpg_fltr, trans %in% input$trans)
>         }
>
>         if (!is.null(input$cyl)) {
>             mpg_fltr <- filter(mpg_fltr, cyl %in% input$cyl)
>         }
>
>         mpg_fltr
>     })
>
>     # create manufacturer input
>     output$manufacturer_control <- renderUI({
>
>         selectizeInput(
>             inputId = "manufacturer",
>             label = "Select Manufacturers",
>             choices = mpg_fltr()$manufacturer,
>             multiple = TRUE
>         )
>     })
>
>     # create transmission input
>     output$trans_control <- renderUI({
>
>         selectizeInput(
>             inputId = "trans",
>             label = "Select Transmissions",
>             choices = mpg_fltr()$trans,
>             multiple = TRUE
>         )
>     })
>
>     # create cylinder count input
>     output$cyl_control <- renderUI({
>
>         selectizeInput(
>             inputId = "cyl",
>             label = "Select Cylinder Count",
>             choices = mpg_fltr()$cyl,
>             multiple = TRUE
>         )
>     })
>
>     # display results in table
>     output$table <- renderTable({
>         head(mpg_fltr(), 20)
>     })
> }
>
> shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
>
>

I am trying to build an interactive Choropleth in Shiny using leaflet. However, the load time and recreate time is really slow. Any way to speed it up. Here is a link to the minimal app folder along with the data: https://www.dropbox.com/home/Leaflet_Shiny_app global.R library(shinydashboard) library(tidyverse) library(ggvis) library(leaflet) library(WDI) library(sp) ui.R header <- dashboardHeader( title = "Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions" ) ## Sidebar content sidebar <- dashboardSidebar( sidebarMenu( menuItem("Interactive Choropleth", tabName = "choropleth") ) ) ## Body content body <- dashboardBody( # First tab content tabItem("choropleth", fluidRow( column(width = 9, box(width = NULL, solidHeader = TRUE, title = "Greenhouse gas emissions (kt of CO2 equivalent)", leafletOutput("choropleth_ghg", height = 500) ) ), column(width = 3, box(width = NULL, status = "warning", selectInput("year", "Year", choices = seq(1970, 2012, 1), selected = 2012) ) ) ) ) ) dashboardPage( header, sidebar, body ) server.R # Read the dataset for choropleth # From http://data.okfn.org/data/core/geo-countries#data countries <- geojsonio::geojson_read("json/countries.geojson", what = "sp") # Download the requested data by using the World Bank's API, # parse the resulting JSON file, and format it in long country-year format. load("who_ghg.RData") function(input, output, session) { # Interactive Choropleth map......................................................... # Reactive expression for the data subsetted to what the user selected countries_plus_ghg <- reactive({ # Filter the data to select for the year user selected who_ghg_subset <- filter(who_ghg, year == input$year) # Merge a Spatial object having a data.frame for Choropleth map sp::merge(countries, who_ghg_subset, by.x = "ISO_A3", by.y = "iso3c") }) # Create the map output$choropleth_ghg <- renderLeaflet({ leaflet(countries) %>% setView(0, 20, zoom = 1) %>% addTiles() }) # Observer to change the color of countries, labels and legends # based on the year user selects in the UI observe({ dat <- countries_plus_ghg() # Define numeric vector bins to add some color bins <- ggplot2:::breaks(c(min(dat$EN.ATM.GHGT.KT.CE, na.rm = TRUE) ,max(dat$EN.ATM.GHGT.KT.CE, na.rm = TRUE)), "width",n = 5) # Call colorBin to generate a palette function that maps the RColorBrewer #"YlOrRd" colors to our bins. pal <- colorBin("YlOrRd", domain = dat$EN.ATM.GHGT.KT.CE, bins = bins) # Generate the labels with some HTML labels <- sprintf( "%s
%g", dat$country, dat$EN.ATM.GHGT.KT.CE ) %>% lapply(htmltools::HTML) leafletProxy("choropleth_ghg", data = dat) %>% addPolygons( fillColor = ~pal(EN.ATM.GHGT.KT.CE), weight = 1, opacity = 1, color = "white", fillOpacity = 0.7, highlight = highlightOptions( weight = 2, color = "#666", dashArray = "", fillOpacity = 0.7, bringToFront = TRUE), label = labels, labelOptions = labelOptions( style = list("font-weight" = "normal", padding = "3px 8px"), textsize = "15px", direction = "auto")) %>% clearControls() %>% addLegend(pal = pal, values = ~EN.ATM.GHGT.KT.CE, opacity = 0.7, title = NULL, position = "bottomleft") }) }

messages.subject: Rendering UI elements

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I am running multiple shiny apps Shiny Server Pro on Ubuntu 16.04. each app is used by multiple types of users, that have different UI's. I found out that rendering complex ui elements via renderUI - i.e. when starting a session - is very slow when using Shiny Server (see https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1175 for more users having this problem). Locally - from RStudio - renderUI runs much faster.

The alternative is loading all ui elements directly when starting a process - so before a session has started. Since I cannot know which user is going to connect to a process before the actual session is started, each process will have to contain all ui elements of all types of users.

You can imagine that this behavior is not preferable (although this is how I "solved" it for the time being). Is there another way of loading ui elements that I am missing? Or am I just not using Shiny (Server) the way it is supposed to be used?

Thanks in advance,

Peter

    Appart_reco<-Base[Base$reviewer_id %in% vingt_voisins,1]
    Appart_reco.DF<-as.data.frame(table(Appart_reco))

    prix_souhaite=100

    Appart_reco.DF<-merge(Appart_reco.DF,Base[,c("appart_ID","prix_quanti")],by.x = "Appart_reco",by.y = "appart_ID",all.x =T )
    Appart_reco.DF<-as.data.frame(unique(Appart_reco.DF))

    Appart_reco.DF$Distance<-prix_souhaite-abs(prix_souhaite-Appart_reco.DF$prix_quanti)
    Appart_reco.DF$score<-Appart_reco.DF$Freq*Appart_reco.DF$Distance
    Appart_reco.DF<-arrange(Appart_reco.DF,desc(score))

    result_reco1<-as.character(Appart_reco.DF[1,1])
    result_reco2<-as.character(Appart_reco.DF[2,1])

    step_result<-as.data.frame(subset(listing,id==result_reco1 |id==result_reco2))

    a<-step_result[1,2]
   b<-step_result[2,2]

  })

  output$reco1<-renderText(a)
  output$reco2<-renderText(b)

}

Thank you very much for your help

Best regards

messages.body_plain:
Hey,

I will try to help you a bit, allthough im still a bit confused about the aim of your little app.
I dont really understand the strike and dip in your exercice and also i dont see where the "data" comes from.

If you could explain in more detail, what exactly your app should be doing and provide some example data we could give more exact answers.

But ill try to help a bit.

First "Strike" and "Dip" seem to be textInputs, so you will get characters from those inputs.
In your first observeEvent you try putting those inputs together. So, data should be c(data, "somecharacter", "somecharacter", nrow=2)
If you type that in the console, you will see that you dont get what you might have expected.

> data <- c(data=1:4, "somecharacter", "somecharacter", nrow=2)
> data
data1 data2 data3 data4 nrow
"1" "2" "3" "4" "somecharacter" "somecharacter" "2"

So, instead of c() you want to use matrix(), as there you can definde the number of columns and rows.

Your second observeEvent waits for the inputButton "plot" and if it is pressed it prints "data", but has no idea what the data is and where to print it.
Similar to your plotOutput you need to define a textOutput, to tell shiny where to print it. And you need to define what the data is and probably use an eventReactive there instead.

I have put you a little scirpt together, which puts that all together a bit.

#######################################################################################
library(shiny)
library(rgl)
#######################################################################################
ui <- fluidPage(

  numericInput(inputId = "n_random", label = "Amount of random numbers",
               value = 10, min = 1, max = 1000, step = 1, width = "30%"),

  numericInput(inputId = "strike", label = "X - Value ", value = 1, min = 1, max = 100, step = 1,
               width = "30%"),
  numericInput(inputId = "dip", label = "Y - Value ", value = 10, min = 10, max = 100, step = 1, width = "30%"),
  numericInput(inputId = "z", label = "Z - Value ", value = 10, min = 10, max = 100, step = 1, width = "30%"),

  sliderInput("size", label = "Size", min = 1, max = 20, value = 4, step = 1),
  textInput("color", label = "Select a color", value = "green"),

  actionButton(inputId = "add", label = "Add a plane"),

  actionButton(inputId = "plotbutton", label = "Update"),

  textOutput("text"),

  plotOutput(outputId = "plot", width = "100%", height = "600px")

)
#######################################################################################
server <- function(input, output) {

  data <- eventReactive(input$add, {
    x <- runif(n = input$n_random, min = input$strike, max = 10000)
    y <- runif(n = input$n_random, min=input$dip, max = 20000)
    z <- runif(n = input$n_random, min=input$z, max = 20000)
    data <- matrix(data = c(x, y,z), ncol=3)
    })

  output$text <- renderPrint({
    dataprint <- data()
    print(dataprint)
    })

  plotreactive <- eventReactive(input$plotbutton, {
    dataplot <- data()
  })

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- plotreactive()
    plot3d(data, type = 'p', size = input$size, col = input$color,

           xlab = '', ylab = '', zlab = '')})
}

#######################################################################################
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

So what it does:
In your UI you ve got 4 numericInputs:
 - for the amount of random numbers
 - for the x-values
 - for the y-values
 - for the z-values

then one sliderInput, where you can define the size of the points in the plot
and one textInput, where you can give a colorname, for the points in the plot.

again two actionButtons, one for the printing and one for the plotting.

and a textOutput and a plotOutput field.

In the Server you have
- an eventReactive, that puts together the data (random x,y,z values) in a matrix with 3 columns.
- the text output in a renderPrint function. It first calls the eventReactive and gets the data and prints it
dataprint <- data()
print(dataprint)

another eventReactive, which waits for the plot button "plotbutton" and gets the data from the other eventReactive

and then the renderPlot function, which calls the second eventReactive, gets the data and plots it.
the inputs input$size and input$color are reactive, so whenever you change them in the ui, they will be changed on the server-side.

If you type a wrong color or you type it too slow, you will get an error, so you may need to add a req() function or some validate() into the eventReactive or renderPlot functions.

I doubt, that this is exactly what you were looking for, but i think it might help you get the basic principles of shiny and R.
As i said, if you have better explanation for your aim and some data to work with, we could help even better ;)

All the best!

#######################################################################################
library(shiny)
library(rgl)
library(plotrix)
#######################################################################################

my_surface <- function(f, n=10, ...) {
  ranges <- rgl:::.getRanges()
  x <- seq(ranges$xlim[1], ranges$xlim[2], length=n)
  y <- seq(ranges$ylim[1], ranges$ylim[2], length=n)
  z <- outer(x,y,f)
  surface3d(x, y, z, ...)
}

f <- function(x1, x2)
  sin(x1) * x2 + x1 * x2

ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput(inputId = "n_random", label = "Amount of random numbers",
               value = 50, min = 1, max = 1000, step = 1, width = "30%"),
  sliderInput("sd", label = "Standard Deviation", min = 0, max = 100, value = 0.4, step = 0.1),
  radioButtons("type", label = "Data representation", inline = T, choices = c("Points"="p",
                                                                   "Spheres"="s",
                                                                   "Lines"="l",
                                                                   "Heights"="h",
                                                                   "Nothing"="n")),
  radioButtons("color", label = "Which column should be used for color representation",
               inline = T, choices = c("First Column"=1,
                                       "Second Column"=2,
                                       "Third Column"=3)),
  sliderInput("opacity", "Surface Opacity", min = 0, value = 0.3, max = 1, step = 0.01, ticks = T),

  sliderInput("size", label = "Size", min = 1, max = 20, value = 4, step = 1),

  actionButton(inputId = "add", label = "Add a plane"),

  actionButton(inputId = "plotbutton", label = "Update"),
  textOutput("text"),

  plotOutput(outputId = "plot", width = "100%", height = "600px")
)
#######################################################################################
server <- function(input, output) {

  data <- reactive({
    n <- input$n_random
    x1 <- 4*runif(n)
    x2 <- 4*runif(n)
    y <- f(x1, x2) + rnorm(n, sd=input$sd)
    data <- matrix(data = c(x1, x2, y), ncol=3)
    })

  observeEvent(input$add, {
    dataprint <- data()
    output$text <- renderPrint({
      print(dataprint)
    })
  })
  observeEvent(input$plotbutton,{
    data <- data()
    output$plot <- renderPlot({
      plot3d(data, type=input$type, xlab="X1", ylab="X2", zlab="Y",
             col = color.scale(data[,as.integer(input$color)], cs1 =c(0,1,1), cs2 = c(1,1,0),0),
             size = input$size, lwd=15)
      my_surface(f, alpha=input$opacity)
    })

  })

}
#######################################################################################
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Re: load table on request via search box
messages.subject_clean: load table on request via search box
messages.body_plain:
Hiya! The following are your friends in this situation: req <https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html>, actionButton <https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/action-buttons.html>, observe, and isolate <https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/isolation.html>. (Links are to the various Shiny articles on those topics.) Here's how one possible solution:

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

header <- dashboardHeader()
sidebar <- dashboardSidebar(sidebarMenu(menuItem(
  "xxx", tabName = "zz")))

body <- dashboardBody(
  tabItems(
    tabItem(selected = TRUE, tabName = "zz",
            navbarPage(
              title = 'zz',
              tabPanel(
                'Customer',

                fluidRow(
                  column(textInput("customer", "Customer", placeholder = "setosa, versicolor, or virginica"), width = 6),
                  column(actionButton("query_btn", "Query"), width = 6)
                ),
                DT::dataTableOutput('iris')

              )
            )
    )))

ui <- dashboardPage(header, sidebar, body)

server <- function(input, output) {

  ctdata <- reactiveVal(NULL) # initialize

  observe({
    # react when user queries using the button, which starts at 0
    if (input$query_btn > 0) {
      # isolate() prevents reaction when input$customer changes
      isolate({
        # this is where you could include your database-querying code
        ctdata(iris[iris$Species == input$customer, ])
      })
    }
  })

  output$iris <- DT::renderDataTable({
    # req() ensures that we have data before we try to display it
    req(ctdata())
    DT::datatable(
      ctdata(),

      rownames = FALSE,
      extensions = 'Buttons',
      plugins = 'searchHighlight',
      options = list(
        dom = 'Bfrtip',
        buttons = I('colvis'),
        pageLength = 25)
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Hope that helps! :D

- Mikhail

messages.body_plain:
If you're interested in interactivity and have a pretty good idea of what types of plots your dashboards will have, then htmlwidgets <http://www.htmlwidgets.org/showcase_plotly.html> like Ger mentioned might be a good bet.

If you're fine with static plots, I would actually recommend ggplot2 <http://ggplot2.org/> as the standard. It has a very customizable theming system, so you can develop a specific theme so your company's plots all have a consistent look. (I would recommend putting this theme into an R package.) There are a lot of ways you can visualize data with ggplot2 core, but it also has a lot of extensions <http://www.ggplot2-exts.org/ggraph.html>. From plotting graphs/networks <https://github.com/thomasp85/ggraph> to survival curves <http://ggobi.github.io/ggally/#ggallyggsurv>.

Hope this helps!

- Mikhail

messages.subject: Async / non-blocking reactives in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Async / non-blocking reactives in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi Shiny Users,

I was recently wondering about the potential approaches to circumvent the synchronous nature of R / Shiny, in particular that a long-running R calculation will block the whole user interface. My first intuition is that spawning separate R processes is the only way to go.

Using the 'future' package I have come up with an asynchronous drop-in replacement to eventReactive, which requires no code change compared to the usual eventReactive and can achieve asynchronous (non-blocking) evaluation. A small gist is available here: https://gist.github.com/andrewsali/3317e5954459fef2f5fed68d68c1ac92

The reason for using the 'future' package is that it takes care of spawning the new R process and automatically exporting the relevant variables by static code inspection of the handler expression.

However this approach also has a few small drawbacks: 1) it's not possible to have side-effects in the handler expression, 2) The reactive produced by my async version will not invalidate downstream when the calculation starts, but instead when the calculation finishes and the value is returned. This means that the 'recalculating' class (opacity) is not applied to an output depending on the async reactive whilst the calculation is running.

The reason why I thought to make eventReactive async is that the event expression (usually the fast part) can remain synchronous and the long-running handler expression can be sent for async evaluation. Also, by creating an async version of a 'reactive' it's relatively a minor issue that side-effects are not allowed for in the handler expression.

I would be very curious to know what others have been doing to have async / non-blocking behaviour in Shiny. Also, as far as I know there is an 'async' version of Shiny being worked on, I would be interested if there is some information on what the underlying approach taken is.

Cheers,

Andras

Hi Dean,

Thanks for the pointer, my gist is indeed very similar to Joe's example, with some additional convenience wrapping (the heavy lifting being provided by the future package) to be a drop-in async replacement of eventReactive.

Given that you also mention a 'proper' async mechanism being worked on by the Shiny team, I would be very curious to hear if that will avoid forking new R processes.

Cheers,

Andras

On Mon, Jun 12, 2017 at 3:21 AM Dean Attali <daat...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I haven't looked at your implementation, and this isn't exactly the same usecase as what you're probably trying to do, but Joe does have a little gist that also tackles a similar problem https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/9504798d93e5c50109f8bbaec5abe372
>
> This gist is from before the shiny team started to work on a proper async mechanism built into shiny
>
>
> On Sunday, 11 June 2017 06:58:12 UTC-4, Andrew Sali wrote:
> > Hi Shiny Users,
> >
> > I was recently wondering about the potential approaches to circumvent the synchronous nature of R / Shiny, in particular that a long-running R calculation will block the whole user interface. My first intuition is that spawning separate R processes is the only way to go.
> >
> > Using the 'future' package I have come up with an asynchronous drop-in replacement to eventReactive, which requires no code change compared to the usual eventReactive and can achieve asynchronous (non-blocking) evaluation. A small gist is available here: https://gist.github.com/andrewsali/3317e5954459fef2f5fed68d68c1ac92
> >
> > The reason for using the 'future' package is that it takes care of spawning the new R process and automatically exporting the relevant variables by static code inspection of the handler expression.
> >
> > However this approach also has a few small drawbacks: 1) it's not possible to have side-effects in the handler expression, 2) The reactive produced by my async version will not invalidate downstream when the calculation starts, but instead when the calculation finishes and the value is returned. This means that the 'recalculating' class (opacity) is not applied to an output depending on the async reactive whilst the calculation is running.
> >
> > The reason why I thought to make eventReactive async is that the event expression (usually the fast part) can remain synchronous and the long-running handler expression can be sent for async evaluation. Also, by creating an async version of a 'reactive' it's relatively a minor issue that side-effects are not allowed for in the handler expression.
> >
> > I would be very curious to know what others have been doing to have async / non-blocking behaviour in Shiny. Also, as far as I know there is an 'async' version of Shiny being worked on, I would be interested if there is some information on what the underlying approach taken is.
> >
> > Cheers,
> >
> > Andras
> >
> >
> >
> >

messages.subject: Re: Async / non-blocking reactives in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Async / non-blocking reactives in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
The eventReactiveAsync() function is very short in my gist, so you should be able to adapt it quickly to your needs. Although I think you can use it out of the box without modifications as well.

The setup is fairly simple (and not too original):
start a 'multiprocess' future (i.e. on *nix based system do a fork of the process, on Windows start a new process). The future package will export the relevant objects to the new process by examining the handler expression.
set up an observer that checks if the results are ready via 'future::resolved()' (note the 'd' at the end, this is a non-blocking check)
if results are ready invalidate with the calculated value the reactive that is produced by the eventReactiveAsync() function.
I am not sure what the advantage is of the 'callr' package mentioned by Dean compared to 'future', as it also starts a new R process. What is nice about 'future' on the other hand is the automatic variable exporting based on the expression to be evaluated.

Cheers,

Andras

messages.body_plain:
Thanks very much Joe. This is my first foray in using Shiny modules and this has been a really good learning experience to start leveraging them, if a somewhat ambitious place to start. I really appreciate your input and thanks very much for putting this together.

On Friday, June 2, 2017 at 9:15:34 AM UTC-4, Garrick McComas wrote:

> I'm pulling a large dataset down into a Shiny app that I only want to pull once with a reactive function and one mandatory filter. Using the reactiveUI framework, I then want to be able to do progressive filtering on the dataset with a combination of several independent selectizeInput(s) such that the available choices are dictated by the selectizeInput(s) already selected. The kicker is that I'm trying to do this without stipulating any order of operations to the filtering, such that any combination of applied inputs would in turn inform available choices in the other available inputs. I'd also like for the user to get back to the original unfiltered dataset by simply clearing inputs.
>
> In the script below, I've simulated this process with one "mandatory" filter that has to be applied before the full dataset is pulled into Shiny nested in a reactive function. The resultant dataset is then nested in another reactive function where the optional and progressive filtering takes place.
>
> Currently the script momentarily applies a filter before reverting to the full dataset, implying that either some sort of recursion is taking place or the initial reactive function that generates the large dataset is being triggered. I've come across a lot of notes about the use of "isolate" that might be of help here, but I haven't been able to figure out how it might be applied in this case. I'm sure the answer to my issue is buried in some post, but I'm having a very difficult time determining how to fix this issue. I would be most grateful for any help!
>
>
> library(shiny)
> library(dplyr)
> library(ggplot2)
>
> ui <- fluidPage(
>
>     fluidRow(
>         # control panel
>         column(
>             # initial input required to query large dataset
>             numericInput(
>                 inputId = "min_year",
>                 label = "Select Min Model Year",
>                 min = 1999,
>                 max = 2008,
>                 value = 2000
>             ),
>             # progressive manufacturer filter
>             uiOutput("manufacturer_control"),
>             # progressive transmission filter
>             uiOutput("trans_control"),
>             # progressive compact filter
>             uiOutput("cyl_control"),
>             width = 2
>         ),
>         # display table
>         column(
>             tableOutput("table"),
>             width = 10
>         )
>     )
> )
>
> server <- function(input, output) {
>
>     # reactive function to pull down large dataset once
>     mpg_all <- reactive({
>
>         ggplot2::mpg %>% filter(year >= input$min_year)
>     })
>
>     # reactive filtering on large dataset that progressively narrows input choices
>     mpg_fltr <- reactive({
>
>         mpg_fltr <- mpg_all()
>
>         if (!is.null(input$manufacturer)) {
>             mpg_fltr <- filter(mpg_fltr, manufacturer %in% input$maufacturer)
>         }
>
>         if (!is.null(input$trans)) {
>             mpg_fltr <- filter(mpg_fltr, trans %in% input$trans)
>         }
>
>         if (!is.null(input$cyl)) {
>             mpg_fltr <- filter(mpg_fltr, cyl %in% input$cyl)

messages.subject: Re: Async / non-blocking reactives in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Async / non-blocking reactives in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
The eventReactiveAsync approach is pretty similar to what I did in the gist that Dean referred to. Andras describes it well. Kudos for figuring out this solution. My gist solution differs in that it uses mcparallel instead of futures, but they're used in almost exactly the same way. Also my solution deals with errors thrown during the task, by propagating them to the reactive expressions; I don't see that in your solution right now but you obviously could add that easily. Anyway, these solutions clearly belong in the same category.

The "proper" async support that's coming will be quite different. I don't have any documentation that I'm comfortable sharing right at this moment--they will probably cause more confusion than clarity at this point. But I will say that the goal is to work with both callr and futures (and no, you won't be able to execute async R code without forking, though you can execute async C/C++ code without forking). It doesn't use the "req(FALSE) until the result is ready" approach; instead, it's much more like JavaScript promises <https://developers.google.com/web/fundamentals/getting-started/primers/promises>, but with 1) a pipeable syntax that's much friendlier to R users, and 2) a novel(?) extensibility point that allows Shiny reactivity to integrate cleanly.

I should have much more to talk about later this summer.

That said, nothing I'm working on should affect your solution--if it's working well for you, I don't see anything wrong with it (other than, it'd be good to propagate errors).

messages.body_plain:
Thanks very much Joe for outlining what direction the async developments are taking!

Whilst eventReactiveAsync works OK in most of the cases (as well pointed out, error handling should be added), a big limitation is that it doesn't integrate nicely with Shiny JS events (an output depending on the async reactive is not in a 'recalculating' state during the async execution). Thus automatic loading notifiers such as shinycssloaders <https://github.com/andrewsali/shinycssloaders> will also not work out-of-the box for outputs that depend on eventReactiveAsync.

Given these limitations, a 'proper' async integration into Shiny will be really great, I am very much looking forward to developments in this area.

messages.subject: Re: Switching between plot and plotly
messages.subject_clean: Switching between plot and plotly
messages.body_plain:
Absolutely do not use eval/parse blindly on user input! Those values come directly from the web browser and cannot be trusted!

I would define outputs on the server for all the possible plot types you want to support. But don't include any of the outputs directly in the UI. Instead use a uiOutput/renderUI, where the renderUI returns the appropriate plotOutput, plotlyOutput, etc. as appropriate.

messages.subject_clean: Reactive Data Frame to Produce Plots
messages.body_plain:
You need to create separate reactive expressions for each of the interesting values that need to change over time (gdp, gen_gov_balance_pc, etc.). And then call those reactive expressions to retrieve their values--you can't just invoke them and then refer to local variables that are inside them. I'd highly recommend viewing the Effective Reactive Programming videos from Shiny Developer Conference 2016:

https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/

function(input,output) { data <- reactive({
  file1 <- input$file
  if(is.null(file1)){return()}
  read.table(file=file1$datapath, sep=input$sep, header = input$header, stringsAsFactors = input$stringAsFactors)

})

output$table <- renderTable({
  if(is.null(data())){return ()}
  data()
})
output$tb1 <- renderUI({
  tableOutput("table")
})

output$modelselect<-renderUI({
  selectInput("modelselect","Select Algo",choices = c("Logistic_reg"="Log","Naives_Bayes"="n","Decision Tree"= "dec"),selected = "Log")
})

output$modelselect2<-renderUI({
  selectInput("modelselect2","Select Algo",choices = c("Logistic_reg"="Log2","Naives_Bayes"="n2","Decision Tree"= "dec2"),selected = "Log")
})
output$employees<-renderUI({
  sliderInput("employees","Select Number of employees",min=1,max= 300,value = 300,step=1)
})

output$tb2 <- renderDataTable({
  if(input$modelselect2== "Log2"){
    f1<-data()
    hr_model1 <- f1 %>% filter(last_evaluation >= 0.70 | time_spend_company >= 4 | number_project > 5)
    hr_model1$left <- as.factor(hr_model1$left)
    train_control<- trainControl(method="cv", number=5, repeats=3)
    # Keep some data to test again the final model
    inTraining <- createDataPartition(hr_model1$left, p = .75, list = FALSE)
    training <- hr_model1[ inTraining,]
    testing  <- hr_model1[-inTraining,]
    # Estimate the drivers of attrition
    logreg = glm(left ~ ., family=binomial(logit), data=training)
    # Make predictions on the out-of-sample data
    probaToLeave=predict(logreg,newdata=testing,type="response")

messages.subject: Re: is R shiny object oriented programming?
messages.subject_clean: is R shiny object oriented programming?
messages.body_plain:
Like most web frameworks, the extent to which you take an OO approach is up to you.  You can implement as much OO using R as you like. See http://adv-r.had.co.nz/OO-essentials.html to learn about R's OO capabilities.

The framework itself just takes care of a lot of the messy stuff involved with creating a web app -- hurdles which are much higher when using R as compared to languages like PHP, Python, or Ruby.

When using Shiny, you simply need to conform to Shiny's API, which is quite flexible.  After that, it's up to you.

output$tbl <- DT::renderDataTable(y())

messages.subject_clean: text wrap in verbatimTextOutput
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
Does anyone know how to enforce text wrap in text areas in Shiny? -- specifically textInput() and verbatimTextOutput()

Here is a reproducible example. I've used CSS to increase the height of the text areas. But "word-wrap: break-word", which is what I thought would induce text wrap, has no effect. Code below. Help much appreciated!

library(shiny)

## demo from Shiny Gallery

## http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/widget-gallery.html

ui <- fluidPage(

 tags$head(

   tags$style(type="text/css", "#text{ height: 200px; word-wrap: break-word; }"),

   tags$style(type="text/css", "#value{ height: 200px; word-wrap: break-word; }")

 ),

 textInput("text", label=h3("Text input"), value="This is a very long string which I would like to wrap."),

 hr(),

 fluidRow(column(3, verbatimTextOutput("value")))

)

server <- function(input, output) {

 output$value <- renderPrint({ input$text })

}

## run

shinyApp(ui=ui, server=server)

thanks, Andrew

This is a general HTML/CSS question, rather than shiny-specific.

A google search for "text wrap in input" led me to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5286663/wrapping-text-inside-input-type-text-element-html-css where you can see that the answer is "text inputs are not designed for that. Use a textarea instead if you want multi lines". It's possible there's some way to workaround that , I haven't looked into it , but I would generally advise against trying really hard to go against what input fields were designed to do because there's a good chance whatever you whip up won't work cross-platform

messages.subject: Re: how to make access to googlesheet work with shinyapp.io
messages.subject_clean: how to make access to googlesheet work with shinyapp.io
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ping, Let me know if this helps. The app below should work once you alter the google login for your settings. As soon as the participant clicks the submit button, their data is added to google sheets instantly.

 First, one needs to setup the authorisation token and a worksheet in googlesheets to use. See below for the setup that works with the app below.

    Note that before this will work you will need to run the following in your console (once installed googlesheets() )
                 1)   ttt <- gs_auth()                                                       # now follow the html. prompts to login
                 2) saveRDS(ttt, "ttt.rds")                                              # then copy ttt.rds file to the app's Dir()
                 3) Now one needs to create a worksheet to use using the following code:

         Data <- gs_new("Data") %>%
                    gs_ws_rename(from = "Sheet1", to = "Data")

                 4) Insert the titles that we want
           Data <- Data %>%
                       gs_edit_cells(ws = "Data", input = cbind("Score1", "Score2", "Time", "Mean"), trim = TRUE)                # Note! you will need to have manually add one row of data to your google sheet otherwise it will error

UI
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(shiny)
library("googlesheets")                                                                                                                                                  # Don't forget to install.packages("googlesheets")
library("DT")                                                                                                                                                                   # Don't forget to install.packages("DT")

shinyUI(fluidPage(                                                                                                                                                          # Open UI
  "survey demo",                                                                                                                                                             # Title

  # Questions
  selectInput(inputId = "Score1",                                                                                                                                     # What we are calling the object
              label = "The Question 1",                                                                                                                                 # Question
              choices = c("Disagree Strongly" = 1, "Disagree" = 2, "Disagree Somewhat " = 3,                                         # Responses
                          "Neither Agree nor Disagree" = 4, "Agree Somewhat" = 5, "Agree" = 6,
                          "Agree Strongly" = 7)
             ),

  selectInput(inputId = "Score2",                                                                                                                                  # What we are calling the object
              label = "The Question 1",                                                                                                                              # Question
              choices = c("Disagree Strongly" = 1, "Disagree" = 2, "Disagree Somewhat " = 3,                                        # Responses
                          "Neither Agree nor Disagree" = 4, "Agree Somewhat" = 5, "Agree" = 6,
                          "Agree Strongly" = 7)
             ),

  radioButtons("radio", label = h3("Do you consent to having your anonymous data stored for research"),                # insert Radio for data storage consent
               choices = list("Sure" = 1, "No, erase all evidence I was here" = 2
                              )),
  # Submitbutton
  actionButton(inputId = "Action", label = "Submit"), tags$hr(),                                                                                   # Create submit action button

  dataTableOutput('mytable')                                                                                                                                      # Data display with downloads using DT
          ))                                                                                                                                                                      # Close Shiny UI and fluid page

Server
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(shiny)
library("googlesheets")                                                                                                                                                  # Don't forget to install.packages("googlesheets")
library("DT")                                                                                                                                                                   # Don't forget to install.packages("DT")
suppressMessages(library(dplyr))                                                                                                                                 # Don't forget to install.packages("dplyr")

gs_auth(new_user = FALSE, gs_auth(token = "ttt.rds"))                                                                                              # login from token file "ttt.rds" in dir(). see post for how to do this

shinyServer(function(input, output) {                                                                                                                           #  Open Shiny Server

Results <- reactive(c(Score1, Score2, Sys.Date(), mean(Score1,Score2)))                                                              #  Create reactive data to input

                                    ##### Function 1, Add data when action button is pressed  ####

observeEvent(input$Action, {                                                                                                                                        #  Observe event action from Actionbutton
  Data <- Data %>%
    gs_add_row(ws = "Data", input = Results() )                                                                                                             #  When actionbutton is pressed this will add their data to the good .doc
                           })

                             #####     Function 2, Create a data display with download option     ####

output$mytable <- renderDataTable({gs_read(Data)}, filter = 'top', extensions = c('Scroller', 'Buttons'), options = list(         # use the Scroller and  Buttons extensions for scroll options and download options respectively
  dom = 'Bfrtip',
  buttons =

messages.subject: Re: Reactive data issue
messages.subject_clean: Reactive data issue
messages.body_plain:
In general, object of type 'closure' is not subsettable means you are trying to subset a function. Reactives are functions, so you need to say summary(outData()).

You'll also need to wrap the summary() in a renderText(), or probably better, a renderPrint() and assign it to a textOutput()/verbatimTextOutput() if you want to see it on the screen.

Also, your reactive will only run once because nothing inside it ever changes.

Tom

I want user have the choice to select value by value but also to choose all values in inputs (by default, i want to show all my table so in filters I want someting like all value of var1, all value of var 2 ... but the all value have to be updated if we choose a filter before. can I do something about the "selected" argument of selectInput ?

library(shiny)
library(DT)
library(dplyr)

VG <- c("A", "A", "B", "B", "B", "C", "A")
AG <- c(1, 2, 1, 3, 4, 2, 1)
AP <- letters[1:7]
AK <- paste(VG, AG, AP, sep = "-")
data <- data.frame(VG, AG, AP, AK)

ui <- fluidPage(
  column(3,
         selectInput("VG", label = h4("VG.ETD"), choices = unique(data$VG), multiple = T),
         selectInput("AG", label = h4("AG.ETD"), choices = unique(data$AG), multiple = T)),
  column(3,
         selectInput("AP", label = h4("AP.ETD"), choices = unique(data$AP), multiple = T),

         actionButton("go", "GO")),
  column(6,DT::dataTableOutput("dtt"))
)

server<-function(input,output,session){

  observeEvent(input$VG,{
    updateSelectInput(session, 'AG', choices = data %>% filter(VG %in% input$VG) %>% distinct(AG))
  })

  observeEvent(c(input$VG, input$AG),{
    updateSelectInput(session, 'AP', choices = data %>% filter(VG %in% input$VG,
                                                               AG %in% input$AG) %>% distinct(AP))
  })

  observeEvent(c(input$VG, input$AG, input$AP), {
    updateSelectInput(session, 'AK', choices = data %>% filter(VG %in% input$VG,
                                                               AG %in% input$AG,
                                                               AP %in% input$AP) %>% distinct(AK))

    data %>% filter(VG %in% input$VG,

  })

  output$dtt <- DT::renderDataTable({
    df()

}

messages.subject: Re: text wrap in verbatimTextOutput
messages.subject_clean: text wrap in verbatimTextOutput
messages.body_plain:
I am not sure that coercing verbatimTextOutput is the right way to go in general. It's supposed to be verbatim rendering of the output string, so that's why it enforces the original line breaks from the outset.

Maybe you can just use textOutput and style it the way you'd like.

For example, put it inside a wellPanel & add monospace font to your output like this:

....

tags$style(type="text/css", "#value{ height: 200px; font-family: monospace;}")

...

wellPanel(textOutput("value"))

messages.subject: Fit xyplot (lattice package) onto screen automatically
messages.subject_clean: Fit xyplot (lattice package) onto screen automatically
messages.body_plain:
I have an application where the user dynamically creates some xyplots from the lattice packages conditional on the data. The "rows" in the graphic layout is configurable. With a single panel, and even with just two rows, my plot seems just fine and visually portrays the information in a way the seems easy to digest.

However, when the layout conditions on multiple variables (typically 3 or more), the xyplot is "squished" in the HTML view and cannot be easily viewed. I have created a minimal example below that just shows one simple plot. Ideally, I would like the individual panels of the trellis plot to be larger.

I hope this is helpful context, if not please let me know if more information is needed.

Can anyone suggest the most appropriate method for filling out the space to display the full xyplot in a dynamic way? By "dynamic" I mean that it would automatically adjust to fill the space depending on the number of rows in the xyplot

### ui.r
shinyUI(fluidPage(

  titlePanel("Hello Shiny!"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for the number of bins
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput("bins",
                  "Number of bins:",
                  min = 1,
                  max = 50,
                  value = 30)
    ),

    # Show a plot of the generated distribution
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("distPlot")
    )
  )
))

### server.r
library(lattice)
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({

    dat <- data.frame(v1 = rnorm(1000), v2 = rnorm(1000), id = gl(5,200))
    xyplot(v1~v2|id, dat, layout = c(1,5))

  })
})

messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to access websockets from within Shiny?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

Did you ever find a good OAuth2 Server workflow using callbacks? I see that in your Google Auth R package, you are using Google's client javascript API to get the token, and that there's an identifier for preserving state. Can I infer from this that you deem the callback-based approach non-ideal?

Kind regards,
Peter

On Thursday, May 26, 2016 at 12:39:49 AM UTC-7, Mark Edmondson wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I currently have an OAuth2 callback that places parameters into the URL of a shiny app, which are read for authentication. The auth flow is actually closing down the initial Shiny instance, going to the OAuth permission screen, then relaunching a new Shiny session with the auth parameters enabled in the same browser window.  This has been working fine, but it's a bit annoying if users refresh the page as the URL is then out of date and it's not obvious why authentication doesn't work. It also means it can't be used in iframes and stuff like flexdashboard, that don't let you access the URL (?)
>
> httr that it's built upon uses websockets to authenticate when working locally, so I wondered if this was also possible when in a Shiny environment.  I'm not clear on how websockets work, and from others I heard it may depend on certain ports being open on the server, but I wanted to ask if it's possible to instead redirect an OAuth to a websockets instead, in a manner that the Shiny app can pick up its URL parameters. That way I can keep a clean URL for users browsers, I hope. :)
>
> Yours sincerely,
> Mark
>

I have an app that uses a DownloadHandler to generate a rather large PDF or word file using rmarkdown. The process can take a while. I have a busy indicator set up that responds to the "shiny:busy" javascript signal that works great for other shiny calculations, but does not get triggered by the downloadHandler process. Is there any way to add that triggering, and also add the shiny:idle once the file has been successfully served?

You can test it at http://shiny.mtbos.org/testing/probgen . Click the "assignment" checkbox the the "Chapter 1" button and see how the busy signal works fine as it generates the assignment in HTML. But click the "download Word" or "download PDF" links and you'll see that the signal does not appear even though there's a good 5-10 second wait.

Thanks!
David

messages.subject: Re: Accessing authenticated user ID from global.R
messages.subject_clean: Accessing authenticated user ID from global.R
messages.body_plain:
I might be misunderstanding your goal, but it sounds like you're trying to perform user-specific actions in global. User-specific is roughly equivalent to session-specific, which means these things must go through the session. The global file is meant for running code that is, by definition, *global* to the entire application - for running code that runs *once* in total instead of once per user. Anything that you want to do *per-user* generally means you want to do that in the server function because it needs to be in the context of every session.

If you give more information regarding the actual usecase, people here might be able to tell you how to achieve what you want. But you can't really do something globally per-user, because that is by definition not global. What happens when two different users access the app at the same time - I assume they shouldn't share the same information?

I hope this was helpful at all rather than just confusing :)

messages.body_plain:
Actually, it looks like even with the pool package I still want an answer to this question :)

Given the following code:

# assumes you have credential info and table name in options()

library(pool)
library(DBI)
library(shiny)

pool <- dbPool(
  drv = RMySQL::MySQL(),
  user = options()$mysql_db$user,
  password = options()$mysql_db$password,
  dbname = options()$mysql_db$dbname,
  host = options()$mysql_db$host
)

ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput("nrows", "How many rows to show?", 10),
  tableOutput("tbl")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$tbl <- renderTable({
    query <- paste0("SELECT * FROM ", options()$mysql_db$table, " LIMIT ",
                    as.integer(input$nrows)[1], ";")
    df <- dbGetQuery(pool, query)
    df
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Every time I run the app, a new pool is created, and the previous ones are not deleted. Running

length(DBI::dbListConnections(RMySQL::MySQL()))

reveals that indeed every successive run accumulates another pool object, and after enough times, I get errors because of too many connections.

I assume this won't happen when the app is served via shiny server and is only happening when I'm running it interactively through rstudio, but I'd still like to know the proper place to disconnect.

You're right, there's currently no way of doing this. We're aware of this, and we're planning on addressing it at some point: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1213 . However, as you've also pointed out, this is not a huge problem for deployed apps because, even though you leak database connections/pools, since the R process is terminated when all sessions are closed, those artifacts will be destroyed as well (even if not in the most graceful of ways). So, the bottom line is that this would be a nice to have feature that we plan to implement in the future, but we also don't think it's a huge priority because, in practice, things "work out."

What I'd recommend for now is:
Don't worry about this for deployed apps.
For interactive use at the console, just run `poolClose(pool)` (or whatever is appropriate) after you exit the app (you can just place this after the call to `shinyApp()` in your script and source the whole file -- instead of clicking "Run app").
Or you can always submit a PR :)

Barbara

Since my previous message we did check again the "Page not found" error and it still happens when someone runs a "too big" query: so while the query runs, the user just doesn't realise it but he's query is preventing anyone else from accessing the app.

So we thought about adding a kill query button but the solutions we found online such as the stackoverflow one below did not always work.
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/15482179/roracle-hanging-how-can-i-cancel-the-query

So by the end we still used the parallel processing and added a time limit to kill it (if the query runs for more than X minutes then kill).

I hope this helps those who get into same challenge.

/Kx

>   # input fields are treated as a group
>   formData <- reactive({
>     sapply(names(GetTableMetadata()$fields), function(x) input[[x]])
>   })
>
>   # Click "Submit" button -> save data
>   observeEvent(input$submit, {
>     if (input$id != "0") {
>       UpdateData(formData())
>     } else {
>       CreateData(formData())
>       UpdateInputs(CreateDefaultRecord(), session)
>     }
>   }, priority = 1)
>
>   # Press "New" button -> display empty record
>   observeEvent(input$new, {
>     UpdateInputs(CreateDefaultRecord(), session)
>   })
>
>   # Press "Delete" button -> delete from data
>   observeEvent(input$delete, {
>     DeleteData(formData())
>     UpdateInputs(CreateDefaultRecord(), session)
>   }, priority = 1)
>
>   # Select row in table -> show details in inputs
>   observeEvent(input$responses_rows_selected, {
>     if (length(input$responses_rows_selected) > 0) {
>       data <- ReadData()[input$responses_rows_selected, ]
>       UpdateInputs(data, session)
>     }
>
>   })
>
>   # display table
>   output$responses <- DT::renderDataTable({
>     #update after submit is clicked
>     input$submit
>     #update after delete is clicked
>     input$delete
>     ReadData()
>   }, server = FALSE, selection = "single",
>   colnames = unname(GetTableMetadata()$fields)[-1]
>   )
>
>
>
> }
>
>
> # Shiny app with 3 fields that the user can submit data for
> shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Re: Any way to run code all active sessions die, similar to on.exit() or session$onEnded() but globally?
messages.subject_clean: Any way to run code all active sessions die, similar to on.exit() or session$onEnded() but globally?
messages.body_plain:
I agree that this is really needed. There are lots of things we might do to mutate some global state that want to be un-done once the app is done running (or even if the app fails to completely launch).

On Wed, Jun 21, 2017 at 3:34 PM Dean Attali <daat...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Thanks, that answers the question in practical terms for this specific usecase.
>
> I'm still wondering if there IS a way to properly implement an onexit-type of function for the more general case
>
>
> On Wednesday, 21 June 2017 18:25:36 UTC-4, Bárbara Borges wrote:
> > Hi Dean,
> >
> > You're right, there's currently no way of doing this. We're aware of this, and we're planning on addressing it at some point: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1213 . However, as you've also pointed out, this is not a huge problem for deployed apps because, even though you leak database connections/pools, since the R process is terminated when all sessions are closed, those artifacts will be destroyed as well (even if not in the most graceful of ways). So, the bottom line is that this would be a nice to have feature that we plan to implement in the future, but we also don't think it's a huge priority because, in practice, things "work out."
> >
> > What I'd recommend for now is:
> > Don't worry about this for deployed apps.
> > For interactive use at the console, just run `poolClose(pool)` (or whatever is appropriate) after you exit the app (you can just place this after the call to `shinyApp()` in your script and source the whole file -- instead of clicking "Run app").
> > Or you can always submit a PR :)
> >
> > Barbara
> >
> > On Wednesday, June 21, 2017 at 11:07:22 PM UTC+1, Dean Attali wrote:
> > > Actually, it looks like even with the pool package I still want an answer to this question :)
> > >
> > > Given the following code:
> > >
> > > # assumes you have credential info and table name in options()
> > >
> > > library(pool)
> > > library(DBI)
> > > library(shiny)
> > >
> > > pool <- dbPool(
> > >   drv = RMySQL::MySQL(),
> > >   user = options()$mysql_db$user,
> > >   password = options()$mysql_db$password,
> > >   dbname = options()$mysql_db$dbname,
> > >   host = options()$mysql_db$host
> > > )
> > >
> > > ui <- fluidPage(
> > >   numericInput("nrows", "How many rows to show?", 10),
> > >   tableOutput("tbl")
> > > )
> > >
> > > server <- function(input, output, session) {
> > >   output$tbl <- renderTable({
> > >     query <- paste0("SELECT * FROM ", options()$mysql_db$table, " LIMIT ",
> > >                     as.integer(input$nrows)[1], ";")
> > >     df <- dbGetQuery(pool, query)
> > >     df
> > >   })
> > > }
> > >
> > > shinyApp(ui, server)
> > >
> > > Every time I run the app, a new pool is created, and the previous ones are not deleted. Running
> > >
> > > length(DBI::dbListConnections(RMySQL::MySQL()))
> > >
> > > reveals that indeed every successive run accumulates another pool object, and after enough times, I get errors because of too many connections.
> > >
> > > I assume this won't happen when the app is served via shiny server and is only happening when I'm running it interactively through rstudio, but I'd still like to know the proper place to disconnect.
> > >
> > > On Wednesday, 21 June 2017 17:37:43 UTC-4, Dean Attali wrote:
> > > > Suppose the 'pool' package did not exist, and I wanted to create a single database connection globally. I'd place the code to connect to the DB in global.R
> > > >
> > > > Suppose I know the app will only have a few people at a time and queries are short and I'm happy with having one connection share between everyone.
> > > >
> > > > What would be the correct way to disconnect from the database?

>

>     sapply(names(GetTableMetadata()$fields), function(x) input[[x]])
>   })
>
>   # Click "Submit" button -> save data
>   observeEvent(input$submit, {
>     if (input$id != "0") {
>       UpdateData(formData())
>     } else {
>       CreateData(formData())
>       UpdateInputs(CreateDefaultRecord(), session)
>     }
>   }, priority = 1)
>
>   # Press "New" button -> display empty record
>   observeEvent(input$new, {
>     UpdateInputs(CreateDefaultRecord(), session)
>   })
>
>   # Press "Delete" button -> delete from data
>   observeEvent(input$delete, {
>     DeleteData(formData())
>     UpdateInputs(CreateDefaultRecord(), session)
>   }, priority = 1)
>
>   # Select row in table -> show details in inputs
>   observeEvent(input$responses_rows_selected, {
>     if (length(input$responses_rows_selected) > 0) {
>       data <- ReadData()[input$responses_rows_selected, ]
>       UpdateInputs(data, session)
>     }
>
>   })
>
>   # display table
>   output$responses <- DT::renderDataTable({
>     #update after submit is clicked
>     input$submit
>     #update after delete is clicked
>     input$delete
>     ReadData()
>   }, server = FALSE, selection = "single",
>   colnames = unname(GetTableMetadata()$fields)[-1]
>   )
>
>
>
> }
>
>

messages.subject: New shiny package - easyslider
messages.subject_clean: New shiny package - easyslider
messages.body_plain:
I started working on a package to make basic shiny UIs a bit more straightforward. The main idea is to map UI components to variables in the dataset, like ggplot2 does for plots.

For example:

   df <- diamonds %>%
     slider2Filter(aes(depth)) %>%
     dropdownFilter(aes(clarity))

   output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
       df() %>% ggplot() + aes(x=carat, y=price, color=cut) + geom_point()
     })

I just wanted to see if there is broader interest in this approach.

Source code here: https://github.com/nfultz/easyslider

-Neal

It looks like the proxy is not allowing our websocket requests to get through. That's not uncommon for older proxy software as websockets are relatively new. You can add the line "disable_websockets true;" (without quotes) in your /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf and reload or restart the server to force Shiny Server to use a different protocol.

messages.body_snippet:
Looks like it's trying to use IPv6 ([::1]) to connect to Shiny Server instead of IPv4 (127.0.0.1), we only support IPv4 currently. Maybe this will help?

https://serverfault.com/questions/527317/disab

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Working with 2 or more selectInput, I had found an odd behavior on Firefox and IE, if you see this example in those browsers you will see the problem http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/basic-datatable.html

When you try to tab over the dropdowns, the navigation won't go further the first one, and investigating further I found as well that the problem is caused if you have more than one parameter on c("All", unique(as.character(mpg$cyl))), For example, if you delete the second parameter "unique(as.character(mpg$cyl)", the tab navigation will continue with no problems. Is this a bug? Have been addressed before? Any comments will be appreciate.

Thank you for taking your time to read.

Shiny app, which is automaticly generated by rstudio when you click (file > new file > shiny web app) doesn't work, turns to gray screen on chrome and rstudio crushes.

How I noticed this is, my own app crushed when I try to add output of a ggplot chart. This template has a basic histogram, I guess the problem is about plots.

#

# Find out more about building applications with Shiny here:

#

library(shiny)

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
ui <- fluidPage(

   # Application title
   titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),

   # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins
   sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
         sliderInput("bins",
                     "Number of bins:",
                     min = 1,
                     max = 50,
                     value = 30)
      ),

      # Show a plot of the generated distribution
      mainPanel(
         plotOutput("distPlot")
      )
   )
)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- function(input, output) {

   output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
      # generate bins based on input$bins from ui.R
      x    <- faithful[, 2]
      bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)

      # draw the histogram with the specified number of bins
      hist(x, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white')
   })
}

# Run the application
